purpose: Substance-first linked audit/refactor: close the gap where storage posture could admit a store with only a tiny positive writable budget even when the caller already knew the expected write batch would exceed it.

changes.change: Admission policy now accepts plannedWriteBytes/minWritableBytes/expectedWriteBytes/requestedBytes and returns plannedWriteFits; reject-planned-write-over-budget gets a bounded warning and is copied into the posture receipt admission row.
Postured OPFS factory rejection detail now carries plannedWriteBytes and plannedWriteFits so recovery guidance is attached to a concrete caller-sized preflight failure.
Probe proves a 600 byte planned batch is rejected against a 500 byte StorageManager-derived writable budget, and that the postured factory rejects before OPFS file creation.
Public types expose plannedWriteBytes/plannedWriteFits and had stale comment tails removed to recover source budget rather than widening the package guard.

riskClosed: A postured store can no longer be admitted solely because projectedWritableBytes > 0 when the caller supplied a larger expected write batch.

budgetRefactor.method: Removed stale public type comment tails while retaining compact cube-audit guard needles after adding planned-write fields.

nonClaims: No runtime promotion, semver change, package publication, production readiness, root tarball slimming, quota reservation, eviction survival, fsync/power-loss durability, Storage Buckets support, Web Lock fairness, or cross-browser guarantee.
